test_title: PYST 3: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 27 Nov, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Mitochondria are special because they have their own DNA and ribosomes. What can they do on this basis?

options.text: Move around the cell on their own
Make food using sunlight like plants do
Make some of their own proteins

solution:
The correct answer is __** Make some of their own proteins**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mitochondria** are known as the **powerhouses of the cell** because they are responsible for producing energy in the form of **ATP** (adenosine triphosphate) through cellular respiration.
 
• Unlike other organelles, mitochondria possess their **own DNA** (mitochondrial DNA or mtDNA) and **ribosomes**, which are similar to those found in prokaryotic cells.
 
• Due to the presence of their own DNA and ribosomes, mitochondria can **make some of their own proteins** essential for their functions, although most mitochondrial proteins are encoded by nuclear DNA and imported into the mitochondria.
 
• The ability to synthesize proteins independently is a feature inherited from their evolutionary origin, as mitochondria are believed to have evolved from **free-living bacteria** through endosymbiosis.
 
• Other functions of mitochondria include regulating **calcium levels**, apoptosis (programmed cell death), and the production of reactive oxygen species as signaling molecules.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Option 1: Digest materials like lysosomes do**

 
 
• Lysosomes are specialized organelles responsible for digestion and recycling of cellular waste through hydrolytic enzymes. Mitochondria do not perform this function. **Hence, this statement is incorrect.**
 
 
 
• **Option 2: Move around the cell on their own**
 
 
• Mitochondria exhibit dynamic behavior, including movement within the cytoplasm along microtubules, but this movement is facilitated by cytoskeletal elements and motor proteins rather than autonomous movement. **Hence, this statement is incorrect.**
 
 
 
• **Option 3: Make food using sunlight like plants do**
 
 
• Plants use chloroplasts for photosynthesis, a process that converts sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide into glucose. Mitochondria do not perform photosynthesis. **Hence, this statement is incorrect.**
 
 
 
• **Mitochondrial DNA**:
 
 
• Mitochondrial DNA is circular and contains genes that code for essential proteins involved in oxidative phosphorylation. This DNA is maternally inherited and plays a role in tracing ancestry.
 
 
 
• **Endosymbiotic Theory**:
 
 
• The endosymbiotic theory explains the origin of mitochondria and chloroplasts as descendants of free-living prokaryotes that were engulfed by ancestral eukaryotic cells.
 
• This theory is supported by the presence of **double membranes**, their own DNA, and ribosomes in both organelles.
 
 
 
• **Protein Synthesis in Mitochondria**:
 
 
• Mitochondrial ribosomes (mitoribosomes) are responsible for translating mitochondrial mRNA to produce proteins needed for energy generation and other mitochondrial functions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison with Nuclear DNA:**

 
 
• Mitochondrial DNA is much smaller than nuclear DNA and primarily encodes proteins involved in energy production.
 
• Most mitochondrial proteins are encoded by nuclear DNA, synthesized in the cytoplasm, and imported into mitochondria.
 
 
 
• **Diseases Related to Mitochondrial Dysfunction:**
 
 
• Mutations in mitochondrial DNA can lead to disorders such as Leber's hereditary optic neuropathy, mitochondrial myopathy, and MELAS syndrome.
 
• Mitochondrial dysfunction is also implicated in aging and neurodegenerative diseases like Parkinson’s and Alzheimer’s.
